statement_record.book: Corel — finite sets as objects, a corelation A -> B being an equivalence relation on the disjoint union A u B, composed by transitive closure of the union and restriction — is a category; it is symmetric monoidal under (empty set, disjoint union); and this monoidal category is compact closed with every finite set its own dual, unit eta_A : 0 -> A u A and counit epsilon_A : A u A -> 0 both given by the equivalence relation whose classes are the pairs {(a,1),(a,2)}.
statement_record.intree: Hypergraph_CompactClosed : @CompactClosed C S with dual := fun X => X, cc_unit X := scfa_delta ∘ scfa_eta : I ~> X ⨂ X, cc_counit X := scfa_epsilon ∘ scfa_mu : X ⨂ X ~> I, both snake laws discharged; together with Cospan_Hypergraph : @Hypergraph (CospanCat C HP) (Cospan_SymmetricMonoidal HP) and Cospan_Monoidal with I := initial object, tensor := coproduct. Corelations themselves are a category CorelCat (jointly-epic cospans) with no monoidal structure.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-stronger in generality on the compact-closed clause (EVERY hypergraph category is compact closed and self-dual, with the cup/cap the book draws, for any base C with an initial object, coproducts and pushouts — FinSet included, via FinSet_HasPushouts); intree-weaker in SUBJECT: the whole symmetric-monoidal + hypergraph + compact-closed tower is carried by CospanCat C, never by CorelCat. Corel is only the jointly-epic quotient of Cospan, and in-tree that quotient is neither a monoidal category nor even instantiated (CorelCat needs a CorelComposable instance, of which there is none).
